topic: Exact-hit information deficiency and minimax design for ranking exact treatment saturations. Fix K≥2, equal cluster size n, distinct interior rational exact-count policies pi_k=m_k/n, iid clusters with unrestricted binary within-cluster interference schedules, and exact-slice welfare targets. Compare fixed-count two-stage complete randomization with iid nominal labels followed by unit-Bernoulli assignment. Let B_kl=Pr(Bin(n,pi_l)=m_k) and q=Bp. Prove the target-tangent lower experiment and local minimax regret bound by holding nontarget-count laws fixed, match it with assignment-calibrated cross-label exact-hit estimation, derive the primitive joint CLT, consistent studentization and rank set, characterize sharp CR/Bernoulli equality and strict-loss conditions, solve the complete two-policy allocation map, and give a certified general-K Gaussian-risk/outer-simplex computation. Use the four-node pi={1/4,1/2} witness and Egger et al.'s Kenya saturation design as consumer; distinguish Han–Owusu–Shin, Joo's downstream Gaussian selection result, Chan et al., and Loomba–Eckles.

open_problems.open_problem: Under unrestricted iid binary interference schedules, does assignment-calibrated pooling of every nominal label that realizes target count m_k attain the target-tangent information bound, and exactly when do optimized Bernoulli-label and fixed-count experiments have equal local minimax simple regret?

source_refs.claim: Appendix B identifies exact-count complete-randomization welfare from Bernoulli data by an IPW estimator that retains only clusters whose nominal label is pi_k; it does not pool cross-label realizations of count m_k.
source_refs.author: Seungjin Han, Julius Owusu, Youngki Shin

source_refs.claim: They derive minimum-L2 off-policy transport weights under Fourier restrictions and show that unrestricted Bernoulli-policy transport falls back to full IPW with a design-mismatch variance penalty.
source_refs.author: Sahil Loomba, Dean Eckles

source_refs.claim: Their ACIC contribution combines Bernoulli-assigned clusters for hypothetical-allocation spillover estimands, but does not give an exact-slice tangent experiment or sharp CR-versus-Bernoulli regret comparison.
source_refs.author: Colleen Chan, Shinpei Nakamura-Sakai, Laura Forastiere

open_problems.why_unsolved: Han–Owusu–Shin's estimator contains the first-stage indicator 1{S_i=pi_k}, even though a cluster nominally labeled pi_l can realize m_k and is then uniformly distributed over the same exact slice. Their result proves unbiasedness and an envelope-based regret bound, not the nuisance-deletion experiment, canonical gradient, or all-rule lower bound. Loomba–Eckles solve a structured Bernoulli-to-Bernoulli transport problem rather than the finite exact-hit map q=Bp. The first missing proof step is to condition on the realized assignment, hold nontarget-count laws fixed in the saturated schedule model, and project the target score; this must also distinguish raw hit pooling, whose variance includes between-assignment mean variation, from assignment-calibrated pooling.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic lower-experiment theorem with efficient variances tau_k^2/q_k, an assignment-calibrated cross-label estimator attaining it with a uniform simple-regret limit, and necessary-and-sufficient equality and strict-loss conditions relative to optimized fixed-count assignment.

writing_exemplar.why: It provides the closest motivation from saturation experiments to ranking exact-count deployment welfares and explicitly separates the exact-count target from Bernoulli data collection.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Saturation experiments compare policy intensities -> deployment welfare is defined by an exact treated count -> Bernoulli implementation hits that count only randomly -> characterize and optimally recover all exact-hit information across labels.

method_exemplars.technique: Use their Radon–Nikodym summation over assignment vectors to identify the exact-count welfare, replacing label-specific IPW by conditioning on the realized count and pooling labels.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It targets the identical exact-slice welfare; the new proof changes which observations carry information and then derives the information projection rather than only unbiasedness.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt their minimum-L2 transport projection and martingale limit argument to the finite exact-count strata, with calibration by assignment-specific conditional means.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems seek the least-variable unbiased transport of an interference-dependent policy functional across assignment laws, but exact-hit conditioning replaces Fourier subspace transport.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack several two-stage causal means, derive their joint covariance, and construct conservative variance estimators and Wald procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its vector two-stage calculations are the nearest established route from several interference-sensitive means to joint inference; exact-hit scores replace fixed strategy cells.

open_problems.open_problem: Can the K-policy Gaussian best-arm minimax game be solved and certified on the full translation-quotiented contrast space, with partial-tie faces and covariance limits, and can that certified risk be transferred uniformly from calibrated exact-hit cluster statistics?

source_refs.claim: Joo characterizes the best-arm minimax-regret rule on a compact hypercube and proves plug-in Gaussian risk results over a compact class of positive-definite covariances; the full unbounded contrast game and degenerate covariance boundary are outside that stated scope.
source_refs.author: Joonhwi Joo

source_refs.claim: Their asymptotic ranking optimality is confined to threshold rules under a rank-one Gaussian structural condition and explicitly leaves higher-rank welfare variation outside the result.
source_refs.author: Seungjin Han, Julius Owusu, Youngki Shin

source_refs.excerpt: The normalized saddle's finite-support geometry and uniqueness remain the dedicated open-ended question.
For J_gen>=3 block-supported response classes with noncommuting within-block Gram matrices

open_problems.why_unsolved: Joo supplies the closest inner decision problem, including general K and covariance plug-in, but states the primal game on [-B,B]^K for finite B and covariance continuity on a uniformly positive-definite compact set. The exact-hit local minimax value instead takes the bound on local contrasts to infinity, quotients out common translations, and may approach partial-tie or shrinking-variance faces while p moves over the design simplex. Han–Owusu–Shin's separate ranking theorem only handles rank-one Gaussian variation. The prior endpoint-Poisson proposal likewise leaves finite-support saddle geometry and uniqueness open, while the higher-rank commitment proposal records the failure of a simple trace relaxation for noncommuting menus. Thus a fitted finite prior or compact-box numerical optimum is not yet a certificate for the full target game; the first changed step is a noncompact minimax/least-favorable-prior limit with explicit tail and face control, followed by a uniform primitive-to-Gaussian coupling.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A measurable attaining or epsilon-attaining selector and matching upper/lower certificates for Gaussian simple regret on R^K modulo common shifts, continuity bounds through partial ties and admissible covariance perturbations, and a uniform LAN/CLT risk-transfer theorem for calibrated exact-hit estimates.

writing_exemplar.why: Its one-shot multi-arm simple-regret formulation is the exact downstream decision object, while its compactness assumptions make the remaining boundary easy to state honestly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: One-shot experiments must choose one policy -> heteroskedastic multi-arm signals make pick-the-winner non-minimax -> Gaussian least-favorable-prior rules solve the compact problem -> certify the full local contrast game induced by exact-hit experiments.

method_exemplars.technique: Extend its least-favorable finite-prior duality, nonlinear Gaussian decision boundaries, and covariance plug-in risk comparison by an expanding-domain and boundary-covariance argument.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired object is the same Gaussian best-arm regret game, but with the compact-box and uniformly positive-definite restrictions removed or controlled.

method_exemplars.technique: Use limits of experiments to prove an all-rule local minimax lower bound and transfer an efficient primitive estimator into an asymptotically optimal treatment rule.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the canonical bridge from a causal experiment to Gaussian treatment-choice risk; the required strengthening is uniformity across several tie faces and covariance perturbations.

method_exemplars.technique: Formulate treatment choice directly as a minimax-regret decision problem and certify least-favorable configurations rather than relying on empirical-success upper bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a decision-theoretic certificate template for showing that a proposed selector attains, rather than merely approximates, the worst-case value.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the exact minimax first-stage allocation for K exact-count policies when Bernoulli labels generate coupled hit rates q=Bp, and can the optimized Bernoulli-versus-fixed-count regret ratio be globally certified over the allocation simplex?

source_refs.claim: They minimize a finite-sample regret envelope to obtain a quasi-optimal saturation distribution, including a Bernoulli-label extension based on label-specific IPW rather than the cross-label matrix B.
source_refs.author: Seungjin Han, Julius Owusu, Youngki Shin

source_refs.claim: They optimize randomized saturation designs for power and document a tradeoff between average-effect power and learning saturation-specific effects, not exact-hit simple-regret risk.
source_refs.author: Sarah Baird, J. Aislinn Bohren, Craig McIntosh, Berk Özler

source_refs.claim: They optimize randomized and deterministic saturation designs for bias and variance under a linear interference model, so the design criterion depends on model structure rather than the unrestricted exact-slice minimax game.
source_refs.author: Chencheng Cai, Jean Pouget-Abadie, Edoardo M. Airoldi

source_refs.claim: The Kenya experiment randomized 68 saturation groups to high and low treatment saturation, making saturation allocation and policy comparison a concrete design consumer.
source_refs.author: Dennis Egger, Johannes Haushofer, Edward Miguel, Paul Niehaus, Michael Walker

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing saturation-design results optimize power, model-based bias/variance, or an analytic regret envelope. Han–Owusu–Shin's Bernoulli objective treats target k through its own nominal label, whereas exact-hit pooling makes every label contribute to several targets through B, so p jointly changes all information coordinates q_k. Once K exceeds two, the criterion is the value of a coupled Gaussian decision game across all local tie faces, not a separable variance proxy. The first proof step that changes is to derive the exact risk as a function of Bp and calibrated slice variances; global design certification then requires valid inner Gaussian-risk bounds at every outer-simplex cell, rather than a non-certified optimizer trace.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient closed allocation map for K=2, general-K optimality conditions, and a branch-and-bound or equivalent certified algorithm returning convergent upper and lower bounds for min_p G(v,Bp), min_alpha G(v,alpha), and their efficiency ratio.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes the experimenter's saturation allocation and the cost of learning several saturation-specific effects the central design problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interference motivates variation in treatment saturation -> learning many saturation effects costs precision -> first-stage shares should reflect the planner's objective -> optimize exact-hit policy-selection regret rather than test power.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate pairwise regret bounds into a first-stage saturation-share objective and solve its constrained allocation equations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It optimizes the same design shares for saturation ranking; the new proof replaces its envelope and label-specific information by the exact Gaussian value indexed by Bp.

method_exemplars.technique: Use least-favorable-prior duality to evaluate the inner multivariate Gaussian minimax-regret problem at a proposed covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: For each allocation p, this is the closest inner oracle; the new result adds rigorous risk bounds and the globally certified outer optimization over p.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt pilot-based variance estimation, constrained design optimization, and oracle design-regret comparison to a coupled exact-hit objective.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It gives a proof template for turning interference-sensitive variance information into an implementable chosen design, although the oracle criterion here is Gaussian simple regret.

open_problems.open_problem: Can calibrated cross-label exact-hit welfare estimates support simultaneous rank confidence sets with uniform coverage over partial ties, covariance estimation, and finite samples in which one or more target slices receive zero hits?

source_refs.claim: They construct marginal and simultaneous confidence sets for population ranks from an available joint approximation, outside randomized saturation designs with hit-induced scores.
source_refs.author: Magne Mogstad, Joseph P. Romano, Azeem M. Shaikh, Daniel Wilhelm

source_refs.claim: They exploit multinomial structure to obtain finite-sample and bootstrap confidence sets for ranks, including categories with small choice probabilities, but the observations are multinomial categories rather than interference-dependent exact-hit outcomes.
source_refs.author: Sergei Bazylik, Magne Mogstad, Joseph P. Romano, Azeem M. Shaikh, Daniel Wilhelm

source_refs.claim: They derive joint unbiased estimators, covariance estimators, Wald tests, and power calculations for vectors of causal effects in two-stage randomized experiments.
source_refs.author: Zhichao Jiang, Kosuke Imai, Anup Malani

source_refs.excerpt: Add a downstream locked-wave inference theorem with a variance-estimation or coverage guarantee
Scoped out of v1: ... a variance estimator / Wald inference for the chosen design.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The rank-inference papers begin with estimators having a usable joint approximation, and Jiang–Imai–Malani derive covariance formulas for fixed two-stage strategy cells. Cross-label exact-hit estimators instead have random hit denominators, assignment calibration, and score components whose availability is driven by mutually exclusive count events; a zero-hit cell makes naive ratio studentization undefined. Partial ties make the rank functional discontinuous where uniform validity is most important. The two adjacent CausalSmith design projects independently stop before downstream variance estimation or coverage, with one reviewer explicitly prescribing such a theorem. The first missing step is therefore a primitive joint influence expansion and uniformly consistent covariance estimate for calibrated hit scores, followed by simultaneous directional testing with a prespecified conservative zero-hit convention.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A joint CLT and covariance estimator for assignment-calibrated exact-hit welfare estimates, studentized simultaneous contrast intervals with uniform asymptotic coverage over every partial-tie configuration, and an explicit finite-sample rank-set rule that remains valid on zero-hit events.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the cleanest motivation for why a plug-in ranking is incomplete and why marginal and simultaneous rank uncertainty answer different policy questions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Policies are ordered by estimated welfare -> sampling noise can reverse the reported order -> simultaneous rank sets state which orderings remain defensible -> construct them for calibrated exact-hit saturation estimates under interference.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert simultaneous one-sided pairwise comparison tests to obtain marginal and joint confidence sets for ranks, using joint critical values.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired output is exactly a rank confidence set; the new input is a calibrated cluster influence vector with hit-induced sparsity and interference.

method_exemplars.technique: Stack cluster-level causal means, derive their joint two-stage covariance, estimate it conservatively, and form vector Wald statistics.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest causal two-stage covariance proof; calibrated cross-label hit scores replace disjoint strategy-cell means.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit multinomial cell-count structure for exact finite-sample rank sets and compare it with large-sample bootstrap inference in sparse categories.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Exact-hit counts are multinomial-like and can be sparse; the new proof must incorporate causal outcomes and assignment-calibrated scores rather than category shares alone.

open_problems.open_problem: How should exact-slice welfare and minimax saturation design be defined and estimated with heterogeneous cluster sizes when n_i pi_k can be nonintegral and deployment must mix the adjacent floor and ceiling treatment counts?

source_refs.claim: Their Assumption 1 requires every n_i pi_k to be integral; they mention a convex mixture of floor and ceiling exact-count designs for nonintegral cases and explicitly omit its analysis.
source_refs.author: Seungjin Han, Julius Owusu, Youngki Shin

source_refs.claim: For unequal group sizes in two-stage experiments, they distinguish cluster-weighted from individual-weighted causal estimands and give corresponding unbiased estimators and randomization variances.
source_refs.author: Guillaume Basse, Avi Feller
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: They jointly estimate multiple causal quantities in two-stage randomized experiments but take the assignment mechanisms as fixed rather than optimize a size-dependent adjacent-count deployment rule.
source_refs.author: Zhichao Jiang, Kosuke Imai, Anup Malani

open_problems.why_unsolved: Han–Owusu–Shin identify the missing regime directly: exact-count deployment at pi_k is undefined when n_i pi_k is nonintegral, and the suggested floor/ceiling mixture is not developed. Heterogeneous n_i removes the single K-by-K hit matrix because each size has different adjacent targets and binomial probabilities; Basse–Feller further show that cluster and unit weighting then define different causal objects. The first changed proof step is to specify a coherent size-indexed deployment kernel and prove that conditioning on size and realized count identifies its mixture welfare; only then can one derive efficient aggregation weights and optimize nominal labels across size strata.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A size-indexed identification formula for floor/ceiling-mixture saturation welfare, efficient cluster-weighted and unit-weighted estimators with joint limit laws, and an optimal-allocation characterization over nominal labels and observed cluster-size strata.

writing_exemplar.why: It treats unequal cluster size as a substantive estimand choice rather than a nuisance correction.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Two-stage experiments naturally contain unequal clusters -> equal weighting of clusters and people targets different welfare objects -> exact saturation may be infeasible in many clusters -> define and estimate a principled adjacent-count deployment policy.

method_exemplars.technique: Average unrestricted potential outcomes over a uniform exact-count slice and transport Bernoulli observations to that deployment law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is the floor/ceiling extension that the paper explicitly omits; one exact slice is replaced by a size-dependent mixture of adjacent slices.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct unbiased estimators and randomization variances separately for cluster-weighted and individual-weighted two-stage estimands with variable group sizes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Those weighting conventions are exactly the alternatives that must be preserved when pooling heterogeneous-size exact hits.

method_exemplars.technique: Express several causal quantities as linear transformations of a stacked mean vector and propagate covariance to joint inference.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A floor/ceiling deployment target is a known linear transformation of size-specific exact-count means, so the stacked-vector proof becomes reusable after deriving size-specific hits.

literature_map:
Han, Owusu, and Shin (2026, arXiv:2606.18590) is the closest paper: it ranks exact-count saturation welfare, derives regret envelopes and a quasi-optimal design, and uses nominal-label-specific Bernoulli IPW.
Its asymptotic ranking theorem is restricted to threshold rules under rank-one Gaussian variation, while Appendix B's Bernoulli estimator does not pool exact-count hits across nominal labels.
Joo (2025, arXiv:2509.03796) solves the downstream Gaussian best-arm minimax problem on a compact mean hypercube and proves plug-in results over uniformly positive-definite covariance classes.
The tension is that the desired local game expands to the full translation-quotiented contrast space and must support certified outer design optimization and covariance-boundary control.
Loomba and Eckles (2026, arXiv:2609.02756) derive minimum-L2 Bernoulli-policy transport under Fourier restrictions; their structured transport differs from exact-count conditioning through q=Bp.
Chan, Nakamura-Sakai, and Forastiere (2023, ACIC) combine Bernoulli-assigned clusters for hypothetical-allocation spillover effects but do not state an exact-slice information or design-deficiency theorem.
Baird, Bohren, McIntosh, and Özler (2018, ReStat, DOI:10.1162/rest_a_00716) optimize randomized saturation designs for power and expose the cost of learning saturation-specific effects.
Cai, Pouget-Abadie, and Airoldi (2022, arXiv:2203.09682) optimize saturation designs under a linear interference model, rather than unrestricted exact-slice minimax regret.
Hudgens and Halloran (2008, JASA, DOI:10.1198/016214508000000292) anchor two-stage partial-interference estimands, and Liu and Hudgens (2014, JASA) anchor their large-sample randomization inference.
Basse and Feller (2018, JASA, arXiv:1608.06805) expose cluster-versus-unit weighting with unequal sizes; Han–Owusu–Shin explicitly omit nonintegral floor/ceiling mixtures.
Jiang, Imai, and Malani (2023, Biometrics, arXiv:2011.07677) give joint estimation and covariance tools for multiple two-stage causal effects with fixed mechanisms.
Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm (2024, ReStud, DOI:10.1093/restud/rdad006) and Bazylik et al. (2025, JoE, arXiv:2402.00192) supply rank-set methods but not calibrated interference-design hit scores.
Hirano and Porter (2009, Econometrica, DOI:10.3982/ECTA6630) provide the limit-experiment route to optimal treatment rules; Stoye (2009, JoE, DOI:10.1016/j.jeconom.2009.02.013) supplies a direct minimax-regret template.
Egger et al. (2022, Econometrica, DOI:10.3982/ECTA17945) is the motivating Kenya saturation consumer; Lu, Shi, and Ding (2026, arXiv:2603.19573) show why between-cluster spillovers limit direct transport of an isolated-cluster theorem.
Targeted searches found no paper using the binomial cross-label hit map q=Bp, assignment-calibrated exact-hit efficiency, or sharp optimized CR-versus-Bernoulli local-regret equality conditions.
prior_proposal_map:
The exact target qid exp_saturation_exacthit_deficiency_design had only state, pipeline, and orchestrator files at scan time; no proposal core, rejected angle, or reviewer JSON existed.
The closest saturation source was banked exp_saturation_skew_threshold/v1; its README and core were checked, but its heterogeneous-spillover and finite-population-variance gaps were not retained because they are less direct for exact-hit ranking.
The accepted exp_design_pm1_exactness_boundary_v1/experimentation core and angle0_v3 review were inspected; its honest scope separately excludes fixed-count covariance geometry and variance/Wald inference.
The active exp_two_wave_endpoint_poisson_minimax/v1 core, rejected angle archive, and reviews were inspected; angle0_v6 strengthening_paths[2] explicitly asks for downstream variance estimation or coverage.
That active core also leaves normalized-saddle finite-support geometry and uniqueness open, providing a prior technique boundary for the general-K Gaussian selector.
The downgraded exp_commitment_price_coupling/v1 core supplied the J>=3 noncommuting response-menu frontier as a higher-rank optimization analogue.
The active exp_mixed_design_degree_frontier/v1 core and reviews were inspected but not emitted because their directed-degree hard-family questions are not direct opportunities for exact-hit saturation ranking.
